entities.title: The HTTP listener has no authentication of its own
entities.summary: Any process that can reach the listen address can use the proxy; the only check is that a request with an Origin header comes from localhost.
entities.impact: Other local programs, or other machines if --listen names a non-loopback address, can send requests through the proxy to the upstream with whatever headers they choose.
entities.workaround: Keep the default loopback address, and rely on the upstream's own authorization header checks.

entities.title: Request bodies sized by Content-Length
entities.summary: The HTTP side needs request bodies sized by Content-Length (at most 64 MiB, with a head of at most 64 KiB), and closes a kept-open connection that stays idle for 60 seconds.
entities.impact: A client that sends chunked bodies gets 411 and the connection is closed; a client that waits longer than 60 seconds between requests must reconnect.

entities.title: Some answers pass through uncleaned
entities.summary: Over HTTP, JSON bodies over 64 MiB, compressed bodies and content types other than JSON and event streams are copied as they are; over both transports, lines or bodies that are not UTF-8 JSON are forwarded unchanged.
entities.impact: Such answers cost the agent their full size.
